note: Three sentences per fund an advisor can copy. Every figure is one the site already shows from the fund's own filing; tests/map/talking.test.ts checks that.

breit.does: BREIT is a non-traded real estate investment trust that owns income-producing property, mostly in the U.S. South and West; its largest sectors are rental housing (42%) and data centers (27%).
breit.risk: Getting money out is limited: BREIT's plan caps buybacks at 2% of its NAV a month and 5% a quarter, and its board can buy back less, or none.
breit.changed: Since December 31, 2025, NAV per Class I share rose 3.6% to $14.65 at September 30, and in the second quarter BREIT sold 126 properties for $2.1B, exiting self storage.

bxinfra.does: BX Infra is a non-traded fund that owns stakes in long-lived infrastructure; its largest named sectors are transportation (29.8%) and digital infrastructure (24.1%), and 58.9% is in the Americas.
bxinfra.risk: Getting money out is limited: the fund expects to redeem up to 3% of its units a quarter, units held under two years give up 5%, and the general partner can modify or suspend the plan.
bxinfra.changed: Since December 31, 2025, NAV per Class I unit rose 13.9% to $31.41 at September 30, and the third-quarter distribution rose to $0.2289 a unit; every redemption request in the second quarter was filled.

bxpe.does: BXPE is a non-traded private equity fund that invests across Blackstone's private equity strategies; 77% of its holdings are in the Americas, and no single sector is more than 13%.
bxpe.risk: Getting money out is limited: the fund expects to redeem up to 3% of its units a quarter, units held under two years give up 5%, and the general partner can modify or suspend the plan.
bxpe.changed: Since December 31, 2025, NAV per Class I unit rose 16.8% to $39.91 at September 30, and the fund program took in about $974.8 million of new money on October 1; every redemption request in the second quarter was filled.

bcred.does: BCRED is a non-traded business development company that lends to private companies, mostly through first lien, floating-rate loans; software is its largest industry at 25.8%.
bcred.risk: The main risks are credit and access: 15 borrowers' loans were on non-accrual at June 30, up from 9 at year-end, and buy-back requests above the 5% quarterly level were filled only in part in the second quarter, as BCRED said they would be again in the third.
bcred.changed: From December 31, 2025 to September 30, 2026, NAV per Class I share fell 5.2% to $23.51, and the monthly payout is now $0.18 a share, down from $0.20 through June.
